## SECTION 0 — EXECUTIVE SUMMARY & OPINION

Curtiss-Wright is a genuinely high-quality aerospace & defense compounder: sole-source positions on submarine, fighter and embedded-computing programs; 12 consecutive years of revenue growth; operating margin expanding from 12% (2020) to 19.3% (Q2'26); >110% free-cash-flow conversion; Piotroski 8/8; negative accruals; net buybacks. The business is not the problem. **The price is.**

- **FY2026 is fully guided** (sales +8–9%, op margin 19.1–19.3%, adjusted EPS $15.10–15.40, FCF $585–605M) — I anchor Year 1 to this. [Actual, company guidance]
- **FY2027 has consensus** (revenue +8.2%, EPS +12%) — I anchor Year 2 to this. [Estimate, S&P Global]
- **FY2028 onward is NOT established by any source** — it is an assumption. I model a fade from ~7.5% to 4% within management's own stated 5–10% revenue CAGR / ≥10% EPS CAGR framework, and I show the full scenario band rather than hiding it in a point estimate.

**Discounted owner-earnings intrinsic value ≈ $386/share (base case), range $237 (bear) to $503 (bull)**, at a WACC of 8.5% derived from a 4.70% 10-year Treasury and 0.878 beta. The current price of **$635 is ~65% above my base intrinsic value** — the market is paying for a decade of ~15% owner-earnings growth at an 8.5% discount rate, i.e., the top of (and beyond) management's own framework, sustained. Even my bull case ($503) is 21% below the market price.

**Verdict: high-quality business, poor entry price. Negative margin of safety (−39%).** Not a buy at $634.99; value zone begins materially below ~$450. (Section 12.)

## SECTION 1 — COMPANY PROFILE & MOAT

- **What it is:** global, integrated supplier of highly engineered products to Aerospace & Defense (~⅔ of sales) and Commercial Power/Process/Industrial (~⅓), through three segments: **Aerospace & Industrial, Defense Electronics, Naval Power**. [Company, company.com]
- **Q2'26 segment snapshot** [Actual, Q2'26 press release]: A&I $268M rev (+12%), 18.4% op margin; Defense Electronics $246M (−3%), 28.0% margin; Naval Power $410M (+7%), 17.3% margin.
- **Moat:** sole-source/long-cycle content on Virginia- and Columbia-class submarines, fighter-jet actuation and embedded computing, nuclear coolant pumps, and next-generation reactor content. High switching costs; decades-long program visibility. Book-to-bill 1.16x in Q2'26; record $4.5B backlog. [Company releases]
- **Demand environment:** FY2027 DoD budget funds three submarines (one Columbia + two Virginia), Columbia funding rising to $15.2B from $9.3B; AUKUS Pillar 1 adds further demand — a genuine multi-year naval tailwind. [Estimate, Defense Budget Overview/CRS]
- **Duration of moat:** high, but defense is budget-constrained by nature — the moat protects margin and share, it does not guarantee the growth rate.

**Basis-change check (continuity warning):** the revenue series is smooth (YoY +2% to +12%, no 20%+ step) across 2014–2025 and matches third-party restatements ($2.50B 2021 → $3.50B 2025). **No basis-change red flag.** Share count declines steadily 49.1M→37.6M (buybacks; "split suspected: False" and FY25 diluted verified).

## SECTION 4 — CASH FLOW & EARNINGS QUALITY

- **SBC is small but real:** $0.022B (FY2025) = 0.63% of revenue — the pack warns it must be subtracted from OCF-based owner earnings; I do (Section 7).

I anchor to FY2026 guided FCF instead, which normalizes it. (This is the single most important data-discipline decision in the pack.)
- **Owner earnings FY2025:** OCF $0.643 − capex $0.090 − SBC $0.022 = **$0.531B**. TTM: ~$0.60B.

## SECTION 5 — BALANCE SHEET, LEVERAGE & CAPITAL ALLOCATION

- **Net debt (my definition):** long-term debt $0.758B + current portion $0.200B − cash $0.371B = **$0.587B**. [Filed]

Including them changes net debt to $0.797B, worth ~$6/share. Immaterial.
  - Investments/marketable securities: not extracted (Section 12 of pack) — if material, they would *reduce* net leverage further; already tiny.
- **Leverage:** net debt/EV ≈ 2.4%. WACC ≈ cost of equity; the balance sheet is a non-event for valuation.
- **Capital allocation** [Company + releases]: M&A is stated #1 priority; 2026 buybacks expanded to ~$260M with $290M authorization remaining; dividend grows ~5–10%/yr but yield is only 0.15%. Net issuance −1.9%/yr (buybacks). Buybacks are value-neutral in a fair-price DCF (dollar leaves, shares fall); I take no credit for them — conservative.
- **ROE 19.7%, P/B 9.3x.** P/B-implied sustainable growth at an 8.5% cost of equity and 19.7% ROE ≈ 7.3% — the market is already paying for high-single-digit sustainable growth in the book value alone.

## SECTION 6 — VALUATION ENGINE SELECTION & CASH-FLOW DEFINITION

**Primary engine — Discounted owner earnings (equity cash flow), 10-year explicit forecast + Gordon terminal value, mid-year convention.**

- **Why this engine:** the company's value is delivered as cash (OCF) that converts at >105% to net income; an earnings-multiple model double-counts the buyback tailwind and requires a tax assumption the pack's data cannot support. An OCF-based model sidesteps the broken tax fields, needs no interest-expense estimate, and is the natural unit of the FY2026 FCF guidance ($585–605M) that anchors Year 1.
- **Cash-flow definition — Owner Earnings (OE) = OCF − Capex − SBC.** SBC is subtracted per the pack's explicit warning (an OCF-based figure that ignores SBC is overstated; FY2025 SBC $0.022B is a real expense). Because interest is already inside OCF and net debt is ~2.4% of EV, this is effectively free cash flow to equity; I discount at WACC (≈ CoE) and net out the small net debt.
- **Cross-check engines:** (1) EV/EBITDA multiple; (2) forward P/E on guided/consensus EPS; (3) FCF yield vs. required return; (4) reverse DCF (expectations gap, Section 10); (5) P/B-implied growth. All five are shown; the DCF is primary.

## SECTION 8 — DISCOUNT RATE DERIVATION

**CAPM:** CoE = RF + β × ERP
- **RF = 4.70%** — 10-year UST, 2026-08-24 (TradingEconomics 4.70%; FRED DGS10 4.69 on 8/20; CNBC 4.72). [Actual, market]
- **β = 0.878** — [Aggregator; vendor states no window/benchmark — flagged]. CW's defensiveness argues a sub-1.0 beta is directionally right.
- **ERP = 4.5%** — long-run US equity premium. [Assumption, standard; Damodaran range 4.3–5.0%]
- **CoE = 4.70% + 0.878 × 4.5% = 8.65%**
- **WACC:** after-tax cost of debt ≈ 4.7% × (1−0.21) ≈ 3.7%; debt weight 3.9% → **WACC = 0.961×8.65% + 0.039×3.7% ≈ 8.5%** (base).

**Sensitivity set used throughout: 8.0% – 9.5%.** Context: the 10Y has risen from ~4.34% a year ago to ~4.70% (dshort), and the stock's late-August pullback coincided with a rate-driven aerospace selloff (StockStory) — a higher-for-longer rate regime argues *against* the bull case's low discount rate.

- **Fair-multiple view:** at 28–32x FY27 EPS $17.13 → **$480–548**; at 28–30x FY26 $15.25 → **$427–458**. The multiples view ($430–550) brackets the DCF's base-to-bull and still sits 15–30% *below* the market price.

## SECTION 10 — EXPECTATIONS GAP / REVERSE DCF

**What must be true for $634.99 to be right:** With market EV $24.04B, WACC 8.5%, terminal g 3.0%, the price requires **~15% owner-earnings CAGR for a full decade**, then 3% forever. At WACC 8.0%/g 3.25%, it still requires **~12–13% OE CAGR for a decade**.

Compare that to what is actually established:
- Company's own framework: 5–10% revenue CAGR, ≥10% EPS CAGR, >110% FCF conversion. [Company]
- FY2026 guidance: revenue +8–9%, EPS +14–16%. [Guidance]
- FY2027 consensus: revenue +8.2%, EPS +12% — **already decelerating.** [Estimate]
- Beyond 2027: nothing on record. [Unconfirmed]

So the market price embeds **~1.5x management's own growth promise, sustained for ten years, at an 8.5% discount rate**. Note that EPS can outgrow OE temporarily via buybacks and margin, but at fair-price buybacks the per-share DCF value is unaffected — the ~15% OE CAGR is the honest hurdle.

**Simpler frame:** at a 2.5% FCF yield and 8.5% required return, the market needs ~6% *perpetual* FCF growth — forever — just to earn an 8.5% return. A company whose revenue historically grows ~8% and must eventually decelerate makes that a very high bar. This is the gap: **the market is paying compounder prices for a growth path the company itself has not promised.**

## SECTION 11 — RISKS & MITIGANTS

**Bear risks (why it could be worth less than my base):**
- **Defense budget normalization / program timing** — CW's moat doesn't set the size of the defense top-line; a budget reset or submarine-schedule slip would cut the growth path. (CRS flags Columbia/Virginia build-rate risk.)
- **Multiple compression** — at 28x EBITDA / 42x forward earnings, any margin miss or rate rise reprices the stock violently (the 52-week range 465–808 already shows ±20% swings).
- **SMR/commercial-nuclear** exposure is real optionality but prototype-stage; delays hit the bull case (not the base).
- **Interest-rate regime** — 10Y at 4.70% and rising directly lifts the discount rate that this valuation is most sensitive to.
- **Concentration** in ~3 submarine/fighter programs; a single-program setback is a revenue event.

**Bull risks (why it could be worth more than my base):**
- Defense supercycle (Columbia + Virginia + AUKUS) plus nuclear SMR transition to production could sustain 8%+ growth past 2030 — my base case gives partial credit, the bull case full credit.
- Margin floor is high and rising (Defense Electronics already 28%); management's top-quartile-margin goal supports 20%+ consolidated margins.
- Strong FCF conversion, low leverage, net buybacks, disciplined M&A pipeline.

**Net:** the range is wide because the post-2027 path is un-established; I carry that uncertainty in the $237–503 band rather than in a false-precision point.

---

## SECTION 12 — FINAL EXECUTION OPINION

**Business grade: A−.** Durable sole-source moat, 12-yr growth record, expanding margins, >110% cash conversion, clean balance sheet, disciplined capital returns. This is a compounder worth owning — at the right price.

**Price grade: F.** At $634.99 the market cap is $23.45B against a discounted-owner-earnings intrinsic value of ~$386/share (base; $237–503 band). The price embeds ~15% owner-earnings growth for a decade — above management's own 5–10% revenue / ≥10% EPS framework — at an 8.5% discount rate, with FCF yielding just 2.5% against a 4.7% risk-free rate.

**Margin of safety at $634.99: ≈ −39%** (base case). There is **no** margin of safety; there is a negative one. Even the most generous defensible scenario (bull, low discount, high growth, high terminal margin) values the equity at ~$503 — still 21% below the market.

**Execution opinion:**
- **Rating for new capital: AVOID / WAIT.** Do not initiate at $634.99.
- **For holders: TRIM/reduce or hold only as a known high-multiple quality holding** — the risk-reward at this price is asymmetric to the downside; a re-rating toward even 30x forward earnings (−30%+ from here) is as plausible as the guidance upside.
- **Accumulation zone:** meaningful margin of safety (≥25% to base intrinsic) begins around **$410–450**; the deep-value zone is ~$330–390 (bear-to-base). If the stock revisits the low-$500s on a defense-budget scare, re-run the model with the 2027 actuals.
- **Catalysts to reassess upward:** management issuing 2027+ guidance or a 2027 investor day with a higher growth target; evidence that submarine/nuclear build-rates are accelerating (funding data) rather than assumed; or a market-driven derating that brings the price to the value zone.

**This is a great company trading at a great-company price. In valuation terms, that is not a buy — it is a sell or a wait.** Numbers before narrative: intrinsic ≈ $386; market $635; act accordingly.
